title: ShieldCare Late Fee: Writing Part of the Fee Off Where a Claim Has Been Decided
content:
Part of a late fee on a Northbeam ShieldCare Protection Plan is written off where the customer has
had a claim decided lately and the plan's cover is running down. Two things are read: whether a
claim stands decided on the plan inside the last 3 months, and the cover left on the plan measured
against the plan's term limit.

**The cover left on the plan** is the cover credited to it, together with any cover put back at an
anniversary, less the payouts booked against it.

| The plan's position | The amount written off the fee |
| --- | --- |
| a claim stands decided on the plan inside the last 3 months, and the cover left is below half the plan's term limit | 6.50 |
| a claim stands decided on the plan inside the last 3 months, and the cover left is at or above half the plan's term limit | 3.00 |
| every other plan | nothing |

### Both sides of the half-limit boundary

On a plan whose term limit is 2500.00, half of it is 1250.00. Cover left of 1249.99 is below half
and reaches the write-off of 6.50; cover left of exactly 1250.00 is at half, which counts as at or
above it, and reaches the write-off of 3.00. Where no claim stands decided on the plan inside the
last 3 months, nothing is written off however low the cover has run.

### A case on hypothetical figures

A plan with a term limit of 1500.00 has 1500.00 credited, 400.00 put back at an anniversary and
1100.00 of payouts booked: the cover left is 800.00. Half the term limit is 750.00, so the cover
left is above half, and with a claim decided last month the amount written off the fee is 3.00.
